s.t: Ruby Turner's cover, featuring Jonathan Butler and produced by Billy Ocean, opened her 1986 debut album Women Hold Up Half the Sky and reached number 30 in the UK.
s.src: Women Hold Up Half the Sky (album) - Wikipedia
s.q: debut solo studio album by British Jamaican singer Ruby Turner, released in 1986 by Jive Records. If You're Ready (Come Go with Me) (featuring Jonathan Butler) Billy Ocean UK No. 30

s.t: The Staple Singers' album Be What You Are, which includes ‘If You're Ready (Come Go with Me)’, closes with ‘Heaven’, on which Jimmy Page played acoustic and electric guitars plus a solo.
s.q: Guitarist Jimmy Page played acoustic and electric guitars as well as a solo on the last song, "Heaven."

f.t: In 1950 group leader Roebuck ‘Pops’ Staples bought his first electric guitar, an amp and the tremolo effect that would help define his sound.
f.src: Forgotten Heroes: Pops Staples - Premier Guitar
f.q: In 1950 Staples bought his first electric guitar, an amp, and the tremolo effect that would help define his sound.

f.t: Roebuck ‘Pops’ Staples's guitar style influenced and inspired John Fogerty, Bonnie Raitt, Ry Cooder and countless others.
f.src: Forgotten Heroes: Pops Staples - Premier Guitar
f.q: His guitar style influenced and inspired John Fogerty, Bonnie Raitt, Ry Cooder, and countless others.

f.t: Roebuck ‘Pops’ Staples spent a while as a vocalist with the Trumpet Jubilees before deciding in 1948 to form a group closer to home.
f.src: Forgotten Heroes: Pops Staples - Premier Guitar
f.q: For a while, Staples joined the Trumpet Jubilees as a vocalist, but in 1948 he decided to form a group closer to home.

f.t: At the 1972 Wattstax festival, in a jam-packed Los Angeles Coliseum, the group was still defined by Roebuck ‘Pops’ Staples's cotton-field guitar sound and backwoods church singing.
f.src: The Curmudgeon: Pops Staples and the Great Variety of African-American Music - Paste
f.q: the group was still defined by Pops' cotton-field guitar sound and backwoods church singing.
